ABOUT

Welcome Message

Dear HKU alumni, ladies and gentlemen, Welcome to HKUAA Choir’s Fall Season that celebrates two classical masterpieces in step with Christmas festivities in December 2026! We are most grateful for your presence and continual support of our choral events. Moreover, HKUAA Choir  is moving forward from strength to strength for the past 13 years entirely due to committed  alumni participation as well as public acclaim! I would like to take this opportunity to thank HKUAA Choir’s music director Dr. Lesley Chan for his voluntary and unwavering commitment in leading the choir to an uplifting level of choral singing and performance! Also talented coaching from Wallace Ng and Kenneth Ma gave assistance to weekly choir practice besides conducting and accompaniment in this concert. Wishing you all an enjoyable evening with resounding music and rapport!

Lucy Cheung
Choir Convenor

Conductor

Vivaldi sets Mary’s song of praise from the Gospel of Luke, a text traditionally sung at Vespers. Listen for the contrast between the imposing opening and the lighter passages, and for the way the music brings the text’s reversals of fortune to life.

Intermission

20:20

April is My Mistress’ Face

Thomas Morley (c. 1557–1602)

Performers
FlashTrack

Published in his Madrigals to Four Voices (1594), Thomas Morley’s April is in my mistress' face is a jewel of the English madrigal tradition. Adapting a four-line verse from an Italian poem by Livio Celiano ("Nel viso ha primavera"), the text playfully traces the progression of the four seasons across the shifting moods of an unpredictable beloved — beginning with the fresh promise of spring in her face and the warmth of summer in her eyes, before cooling into autumn in her bosom and ending in the chill of "a cold December" in her heart. Morley matches this seasonal journey with deft musical word painting and sparkling rhythmic vitality, contrasting bright, nimble vocal interplay at the opening with slower, frost-tinged harmonies at the close.

Ave Verum Corpus

Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (1756–1791)

Performers
FlashTrack

Toward the end of his life, Mozart wrote one of the simplest and most perfect works of his extraordinary career: a setting of the hymn Ave verum corpus. Composed in June 1791, less than six months before his death, the piece was written for Anton Stoll, the choirmaster of the parish church in Baden near Vienna, for the Feast of Corpus Christi. Setting a 14th-century Latin Eucharistic hymn (often attributed to Pope Innocent VI), the motet contemplates Christ’s sacrifice on the cross and asks for grace in the final hour of life. Spanning just forty-six bars, the work is a masterpiece of late-period simplicity and spiritual serenity.

Drop, Drop, Slow Tears

Orlando Gibbons (1583–1625)

Performers
FlashTrack

First published in 1623, Drop, drop, slow tears sets a poignant devotional poem by Phineas Fletcher and is a short, deeply moving English Renaissance sacred madrigal about penitence, spiritual humility, and seeking forgiveness from God. In three brief stanzas, the poet urges his tears to fall endlessly to wash away his "faults and fears," offering his sorrow as a path to spiritual renewal. The work pairs Fletcher’s sorrowful verse of repentance with Gibbons’s understated, harmonically rich hymn tune. It opens with descending melodic motifs that mimic falling tears, unfolding through tender suspensions that evoke both human contrition and quiet hope. Traditionally performed during Lent or Passiontide, this miniature masterpiece offers a moment of quiet introspection and grace.

20:40

Nelson Mass

Joseph Haydn (1732–1809)

Conductor
Kenneth MA
Pianist
Wallace NG
Performers
HKUAA Choir

Haydn wrote this late Mass in 1798 and titled it Missa in angustiis, often translated as “Mass for troubled times.” The urgent D-minor opening gives way by the end to a D-major prayer for peace.

LYRICS

MagnificatAntonio Vivaldi

Latin

Magníficat ánima mea Dóminum. Et exultávit spíritus meus: in Deo salutári meo. Quia respéxit humilitátem ancíllae suae: Ecce enim ex hoc beátam me dicent omnes generatiónes. Quia fécit mihi mágna qui pótens est: et sánctum nómen eius. Et misericórdia eius in progénies et progénies timéntibus eum. Fécit poténtiam in bráchio suo: dispérsit supérbos mente cordis sui. Depósuit poténtes de sede: et exaltávit húmiles. Esuriéntes implévit bonis: et dívites dimísit inánes. Suscépit Ísrael púerum suum: recordátus misericórdiae suae. Sicut locútus est ad patres nostros: Ábraham, et sémini eius in saecula. Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto, Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sæcula sæculórum. Amen.

English

My soul doth magnify the Lord. My spirit hath rejoiced in God my Savior. For He hath regarded the lowliness of His meek hand-maiden: For behold from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed. He that hath thus magnified me is great in might; His name is holy. And He showeth mercy to them that fear Him throughout all time and every age. He hath shown His strength, His arm’s mighty power: He scattered the proud ones in their heart’s desiring. He hath put down the mighty from their seats of priviledge, and hath exalted the meek. The hungry people He hath sustained; the rich He hath sent empty away. His servant Israel He hath sustained, in remembrance of His great mercy: As it was promised our fore-fathers, to Abraham and his seed for evermore. Glory be the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, As it was in the beginning, so is now, and forever shall be. Amen.

English text adapted from “A Kalmus Classic Edition K06498: Magnificat by Antonio VIVALDI, edited and translated by Clayton Westermann”

April is My Mistress’ FaceThomas Morley

April is in my mistress' face, And July in her eyes hath place; Within her bosom is September, But in her heart a cold December.

Ave Verum CorpusWolfgang Amadeus Mozart

Latin

Ave verum corpus, Natum de Maria Virgine, Vere passum, immolatum In cruce pro homine, Cujus latus perforatum Unda fluxit et sanguine, Esto nobis praegustatum In mortis examine.

English

Hail, true Body, Born of the Virgin Mary, Truly suffered, sacrificed On the cross for mankind, From whose pierced side Flowed water and blood: Be for us a foretaste [of the Heavenly banquet] In the trial of death.

English text adapted from Ave verum corpus - Wikipedia

Drop, Drop, Slow TearsOrlando Gibbons

Drop, drop, slow tears, And bathe those beauteous feet Which brought from Heaven The news and Prince of Peace. Cease not, wet eyes, His mercy to entreat; To cry for vengeance Sin doth never cease. In your deep floods Drown all my faults and fears; Nor let His eye See sin, but through my tears.

Nelson MassJoseph Haydn

Kyrie

Latin

Kyrie eleison. Christe eleison. Kyrie eleison.

English

Lord, have mercy upon us. Christ, have mercy upon us. Lord, have mercy upon us.

Gloria

Latin

Gloria in excelsis Deo, et in terra pax hominibus bonae voluntatis. Laudamus te. Adoramus te. Benedicimus te. Glorificamus te. Gratias agimus tibi propter magnam gloriam tuam. Domine Deus, rex coelestis, Deus Pater omnipotens. Domine Fili unigenite, Jesu Christe. Domine Deus, Agnus Dei, Filius Patris: Qui tollis peccata mundi, miserere nobis. Qui tollis peccata mundi, suscipe deprecationem nostram. Qui sedes ad dexteram Patris, miserere nobis. Quoniam tu solus sanctus, tu solus Dominus, tu solus altissimus: Jesu Christe, cum Sancto Spiritu, in gloria Dei Patris. Amen.

English

Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, goodwill toward men. We praise thee. We adore thee. We bless thee. We glorify thee. We give thanks to thee on account of thy great glory. Lord God, king of heaven, God the omnipotent Father. Lord the only begotten Son, Jesus Christ. Lord God, Lamb of God, Son of the Father: Who takest away the sins of the world, have mercy upon us. Who takest away the sins of the world, hear our prayer. Who sittest at the right hand of the Father, have mercy upon us. For thou alone art holy, thou alone art God, thou alone art most high: Jesus Christ, with the Holy Ghost, in the glory of God the Father. Amen.

Sanctus

Latin

Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus, Dominus Deus Sabaoth. Pleni sunt coeli et terra gloria tua. Hosanna in excelsis.

English

Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord God of Hosts. Heaven and earth are full of thy glory. Hosanna in the highest.

Benedictus

Latin

Benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini. Hosanna in excelsis.

English

Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. Hosanna in the highest.

Agnus Dei

Latin

Agnus Dei, qui tollis peccata mundi, miserere nobis. Agnus Dei, qui tollis peccata mundi, dona nobis pacem.

English

Lamb of God, who takest away the sins of the world, have mercy on us. Lamb of God, who takest away the sins of the world, grant us peace.

ARTISTS

Photolesley.pngHonorary Music Director and ConductorDr. Lesley Ka-Hei CHAN

Dr. Chan is a dedicated music educator, composer, and conductor with over 20 years of experience in the choral music scene. He has been a passionate advocate for arts education, collaborating with schools, professional arts groups, and organizations that support the arts. After completing his undergraduate studies at the University of Hong Kong (HKU), Dr. Chan researched on the Russian composer - Prokofiev's piano transcriptions and attained MMus (Historical Musicology) from the University of London. Upon returning to Hong Kong, he furthered his interest in music composition at the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts (HKAPA) and The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK). His doctoral thesis focused on Chinese choral compositions. Committed to lifelong learning, he is currently pursuing additional studies in business and law while managing a busy professional schedule. In his choral conducting career, Dr. Chan has led youth and amateur choirs to success in several prestigious international competitions, including the Overall Championship at the International Choral Kathaumixw in British Columbia, Canada, in 2016, and the 34th Takarazuka International Chamber Choir Contest in Japan in 2018. He has also conducted opera choruses for productions directed by Professor Lo King-man, including Carmen, La Bohème, Madame Butterfly, The Merry Widow, and Norma. Currently, he is dedicated to mentoring several alumni choirs on a voluntary basis, expressing his gratitude to his alma maters.

Photowallace.pngAssistant Music Director and PianistWallace Chi-Ho NG

Wallace Ng is a pianist and choral musician who frequently serves as accompanist for school and community choirs, as well as for individual students in rehearsals, examinations and performances. During his student years, he participated in local competitions and won prizes at the Hong Kong Schools Music Festival, including the senior piano four‑hands category. Drawing on his work as a secondary school music teacher and choir conductor, he is particularly attentive to supporting singers' breathing, diction and ensemble in performance, aiming to provide a sensitive and reliable musical foundation from the piano.

Photokenneth.pngConductor and PianistKenneth Wing-Heng MA

Kenneth Ma is a Hong Kong choral conductor and social entrepreneur. He graduated from the University of Hong Kong, majoring in Business and Music. A prize-winning conductor, he was awarded the "Most Promising Conductor Award" at the 2nd International Choral Conductors' Competition in Preveza in 2025, and has received full scholarships to participate in several internationally renowned conducting masterclasses, including the Vienna Opera Academy, the Taipei International Choral Festival and the Dohnányi Academy. During his tenure as Choirmaster of the University Choir of HKU, Kenneth led the ensemble to win the Champion Award at the 76th Hong Kong Schools Music Festival and capture a Silver Award at the Singapore International Choral Festival. He also premiered the Dvořák Mass in D, bringing together over 80 performers on stage. His leadership also included conducting HKU's University Philharmonic Orchestra and Choir for the Inauguration Ceremony, as well as promoting various cross-regional musical exchanges. Kenneth is the Co-founder and Music Director of Luff Chorus, dedicating himself to promoting choral culture in Hong Kong. He also founded the social innovation music project 'Embrace Chorus', providing music services for patients with dementia. Currently, he serves as Assistant Conductor and Pianist for the HKUAA Choir and the Cecilian Singers. A pianist since childhood, Kenneth holds an LTCL Diploma in Piano Performance with Distinction from Trinity College London. He has studied under Prof. Hollerung Gabor, Prof. Uroš Lajovic, Prof. Toby Purser, Dr. Jerome Hoberman, Dr. Mary Wu, Mr. Sanders Lau, Mr. Angus Lee and Mr. Felix Yeung. His musicianship reflects both artistic excellence and a strong social mission, rooted in a deep belief in music's power to connect people and build community.

Photohelen.pngSopranoHelen TE

Helen Te obtained her Master of Music degree from the Royal Northern College of Music with Scholarship. She has been invited to perform as a soloist in Schubert's Mass in A-flat major, Fauré’s Requiem and Mozart’s Coronation Mass with the Pro-Musica society of Hong Kong. Operatic roles included Lola in Cavalleria Rusticana at the Hanoi Opera House, Suor Dolcina in Suor Angelica, Frasquita in Carmen, La Cecchina in La Buona Figliola, Laetitia in The Old Maid and the Thief, Dido in Dido and Aeneas. As an educator, she has led Hong Kong singers to Beijing and participated in the International Children’s day Show at the National Centre for the Performing Arts. She is also the choir conductor of the ESF International Schools and participated in the ESF Choral concerts held at the Queen Elizabeth Stadium.

Photosamantha.pngMezzo-sopranoSamantha CHONG

Samantha Chong is one of the leading mezzo-sopranos in the Asia-Pacific region. She is the winner of the inaugural ASEAN Vocal Competition held in 2016. After graduating from the Hong Kong Academy of Performing Arts, she jump-started her career as a soloist with the Hong Kong Philharmonic Orchestra, Opera Hong Kong, Hong Kong Grand Opera, the Hong Kong Arts Festival, and Musica Viva. Samantha made her Italian debut in 2019 at Teatro Petruzzelli, singing Rosina in Il Barbiere di Siviglia. In 2023, she performed at the opening concert of the Edinburgh International Festival, singing Tan Dun's Buddha Passion. Over the years, she has performed internationally with numerous orchestras, notably Singapore Lyric Opera, Kuala Lumpur City Opera, Royal Scottish National Orchestra, Vancouver Symphony Orchestra, Orquesta Nacional de España, and many more.

Photodennis.pngTenorDennis LAU

Dennis Lau, a Hong Kong-born tenor, studied voice with Italian soprano Isabel Gentile and baritone Roberto Abbondanza. After obtaining a Bachelor of Arts (Hon) in music, he then furthered his study in chamber singing at the Istituto Superiore di Studi Musicali "G. Briccialdi" of Terni, Italy. Since he graduated, he has performed different roles in numerous opera productions, including Nemorino in Donizetti’s L’elisir d’amore, Arturo in Lucia di Lammermoor, Hervey in Anna Bolena, Sesto in Handel’s Giulio Cesare, Don Ottavio in Don Giovanni, Podestà in La Finta Giardiniera, Fracasso in La Finta Semplice, Ferrando in Così fan tutte, Mitridate in Mitridate: Re di Ponto, Tito in La Clenmenza di Tito, Silla in Lucio Silla by Mozart, Le Remendao in Bizet’s Carmen, etc. He has been invited to sing as a soloist in many concerts, including Beethoven’s Symphony No. 9, Bruckner’s Te Deum, Haydn’s The Creation, Schubert’s Mass in A-flat major, and Mendelssohn’s Elijah in semi-staged opera form. Apart from singing, Dennis is also very active as a choral conductor. He is currently the conductor for Shaw College Choir, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Wah Yan College, Kowloon Intermediate Choir, Pun U Association Wah Yan Primary School, King’s College and Fukien Secondary School (Siu Sai Wan). He is currently the Music Director of The Hong Kong Women’s Choir and Chorus Master of Musica Viva.

Photogabriel.pngTenorGabriel MA

Tenor Gabriel Ma is an active presence on Hong Kong's operatic and concert stages. In September 2026, he sang Aufidio in the Asian premiere of Musica Viva's production of Mozart's Lucio Silla, having previously appeared with the company as Normanno in Donizetti's Lucia di Lammermoor and as Arbate in Mozart's Mitridate, re di Ponto. Other roles include Goro in Madama Butterfly, Dr. Blind in Die Fledermaus, Monostatos in Die Zauberflöte, Don Curzio and Don Basilio in Le nozze di Figaro, and Gelindo in Cimarosa's L'impresario in angustie (cover). In 2003, he became Hong Kong's first boy soprano to perform in The Snowman, and the City Chamber Orchestra of Hong Kong twice invited him to sing the tenor solo in Blake's The Bear, marking the twentieth anniversary of his stage debut. In December 2023, he performed songs from Schubert's Winterreise with pianist Dr. Helen Cha. Ma trained at the Jacobs School of Music, Indiana University (Master of Music in Vocal Performance with an Outside Area in Choral Conducting), and holds a Master of Arts in Arts Administration.

Photokwok-ho.pngBaritoneKwok-Ho LAM

Lam Kwok Ho has performed in opera productions by Opera Hong Kong and the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts. His operatic credits include Sciarrone in Tosca, Somnus in Semele, Marco and the title role of Gianni Schicchi, Lindorf/ Coppélius/ Dr. Miracle/ Daperdutto in Les contes d’Hoffmann. As a concert soloist, he has performed Beethoven’s Choral Fantasy and Bach’s Christmas Oratorio under the baton of Helmuth Rilling. His recent performance includes Guglielmo in Cosi fan Tutte (Taiwan). He obtained his Bachelor of Business Administration degree from the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology. With support of Cecil Leong Scholarship, Michael Rippon Memorial Scholarship and Fung Kit Ling Scholarship, he received his Advanced Diploma and Master of Music degree from the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts under the tutelage of renowned soprano Nancy Yuen. He has participated in masterclasses by Nelly Miricioiu, Renée Fleming, Eric Halfvarson, Thomas Quasthoff, Dennis O’Neill, Rudolf Piernay, Wolfgang Brendel and Helen Donath. He is currently a vocal teacher at the HKAPA Junior Music Programme.

CHOIR

Hong Kong University Alumni Association Choir

About the Choir

Established in March 2013 as a sub-committee of the Hong Kong University Alumni Association (HKUAA), the HKUAA Choir presents four to six concerts annually across Hong Kong. Collaborating regularly with leading musicians, the Choir is committed to high-quality performances and expanding choral appreciation. Notable highlights include the March 2015 performance of Mozart' s Requiem with the Hong Kong Medical Association Orchestra at the HKAPA which was among the Choir' s most representative works; the April 2018 Messiah Charity Concert, the Choir' s first major fundraising event for designated charities; and July 2022’s Rhythm of the Earth concert at the Hong Kong Cultural Centre, conducted by Professor Chan Wing Wah alongside the Hong Kong Chinese Orchestra and other choirs. In 2023 the Choir joined charity concerts organized by the SAR Philharmonic Orchestra, performing Beethoven' s Symphony No. 9 (Ode to Joy) and Borodin's Polovtsian Dances from Prince Igor. In December 2023 the Choir held its Tenth‑Anniversary Messiah Concert. In November 2024 the Choir collaborated with choristers from Vancouver for the Harmony Across Timeless Music concert, presenting the Yellow River Cantata and beloved Cantonese songs. In April 2025 the Choir was invited by the SAR Philharmonic Orchestra to perform Fauré' s Requiem in charity concerts. The HKUAA Choir continues to unite alumni through music, broaden its repertoire, and share uplifting performances with audiences across Hong Kong.

FlashTrack

FlashTrack was founded in 2018 by a group of choral singers from the HKUAA Choir who shared a passion for music and a desire to expand their repertoire and vocal abilities. Over the years, FlashTrack has performed in various concerts organized by the HKUAA Choir, demonstrating its versatility across both mixed-voice (SATB) and treble-voice (SSAA) ensembles. Under the guidance and coaching of Mr. Raoul Chan, the group continually strives to refine its vocal technique and musicality across a diverse repertoire. FlashTrack warmly welcomes singers eager to explore the world of a cappella singing and dedicate themselves to blending their voices into a cohesive ensemble.
